rationale:
Split into two children. Fully formalized, the supplied proof of bf_coneMass_ball_le is about 255 Lean lines. It contains two self-contained, reusable obligations that do not depend on the hypotheses on B.

(1) slab_cover is the geometric core of Mattila Lemma 15.14 (supplied Steps 3–4): the sup-radius h(x), the far cone point x′, and the inclusion of the slab {|P(z − x)| < s h/4} into {x} ∪ two s-cones of radius 3h. It is stated for an arbitrary continuous linear P and an arbitrary set S.

(2) ball_packing is fact (F2) plus Step 7. On an n-dimensional subspace W, Hⁿ(W ∩ B(v, r)) = ω rⁿ with 0 < ω < ∞. Hence a countable disjoint family of balls centred in W and lying inside B(w₀, R) has Σρⁿ ≤ Rⁿ.

The parent keeps these steps:
- Step 2: the cone-free remainder E = B′ ∖ B″ is null, by the existing resolved sibling bf_coneFree_countablyRectifiable (applied with s/4 and r = 1) plus PurelyUnrectifiable.
- Step 5: slab mass, via (H) at x and at x′ with r = 3h(x) < δ, and Hⁿ{x} = 0 from Measure.nullSingletonClass_hausdorff.
- Step 6: Vitali covering, via Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement with τ = 2, and Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_isOpen. A separate vitali_cover child was drafted, then merged back after independent review because it is a 13-line wrapper around one Mathlib call.
- Steps 8–9: summation.

How the children give the parent by the supplied proof:
1. For each x ∈ B″, apply slab_cover with P := W.starProjection, S := B′ = B ∩ B(a, δ/8) and R := δ/4 (|y − x| < δ/4 on B′). This gives h(x) ∈ (0, δ/4], x′(x) ∈ B′ ⊆ B and the slab inclusion.
2. Step 5 then gives Hⁿ(B′ ∩ C_x) ≤ 2c(3h(x)s)ⁿ.
3. Vitali on the balls B(Px, s h(x)/20) gives a countable T ⊆ B″ with B″ ⊆ ⋃_{t∈T} B′ ∩ C_t, since |Px − Pt| < 3 s h(t)/20 < s h(t)/4.
4. Apply ball_packing with w := P, ρ := s h/20, w₀ := Pa ∈ W and R := δ/4. Its hypotheses hold because |Pt − Pa| ≤ |t − a| < δ/8 and s h(t)/20 < δ/80. This gives Σ_{t∈T}(s h(t)/20)ⁿ ≤ (δ/4)ⁿ.
5. Hence Hⁿ(B ∩ B(a, δ/8)) ≤ Hⁿ(B″) ≤ 2c·60ⁿ(δ/4)ⁿ = 2·15ⁿcδⁿ.

subproblems.title: The slab around a cone point is covered by two cones (Mattila 15.14, steps 3–4)
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, P : ℝ^N → ℝ^N a continuous linear map, s > 0, R ∈ ℝ, S ⊆ ℝ^N and x ∈ ℝ^N. Assume some y ∈ S satisfies |P(y − x)| < (s/4)|y − x|, and |y − x| ≤ R for every y ∈ S. Then there exist h ∈ ℝ with 0 < h ≤ R and x′ ∈ S such that S ∩ {z : |P(z − x)| < s·h/4} ⊆ {x} ∪ ({y : |P(y − x)| < s|y − x|} ∩ B(x, 3h)) ∪ ({y : |P(y − x′)| < s|y − x′|} ∩ B(x′, 3h)), where B(v, ρ) is the open ball and |·| the Euclidean norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (P : Rn N →L[ℝ] Rn N) (s R : ℝ) (S : Set (Rn N)) (x : Rn N), 0 < s → (∃ y ∈ S, ‖P (y - x)‖ < s / 4 * ‖y - x‖) → (∀ y ∈ S, ‖y - x‖ ≤ R) → ∃ h : ℝ, 0 < h ∧ h ≤ R ∧ ∃ x' ∈ S, S ∩ {z | ‖P (z - x)‖ < s * h / 4} ⊆ insert x ({y | ‖P (y - x)‖ < s * ‖y - x‖} ∩ Metric.ball x (3 * h) ∪ {y | ‖P (y - x')‖ < s * ‖y - x'‖} ∩ Metric.ball x' (3 * h))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is Steps 3–4 of the parent proof of bf_coneMass_ball_le (P. Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces, Lemma 15.14; M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch–Federer Projection Theorem, Lemma 4.6). It is extracted for an arbitrary continuous linear map P and an arbitrary set S; in the parent, P = W.starProjection, S = B ∩ B(a, δ/8) and R = δ/4. Only the linearity of P and s > 0 are used.

Claim. Let N ∈ ℕ, P : ℝ^N → ℝ^N continuous linear, s > 0, R ∈ ℝ, S ⊆ ℝ^N and x ∈ ℝ^N. Assume some y ∈ S has |P(y − x)| < (s/4)|y − x|, and |y − x| ≤ R for all y ∈ S. Then there are h with 0 < h ≤ R and x′ ∈ S such that S ∩ {z : |P(z − x)| < s·h/4} ⊆ {x} ∪ ({y : |P(y − x)| < s|y − x|} ∩ B(x, 3h)) ∪ ({y : |P(y − x′)| < s|y − x′|} ∩ B(x′, 3h)).

Notation.
- |·| is the Euclidean norm.
- B(v, ρ) := {y : |y − v| < ρ} is the open ball (Metric.ball v ρ).
- For v ∈ ℝ^N and t > 0, X_∞(v, t) := {y : |P(y − v)| < t|y − v|}.
- Linearity of P gives P(0) = 0 and P(u − v) = P(u) − P(v).

1. Cone points. Let Y := {y ∈ S : |P(y − x)| < (s/4)|y − x|}. By hypothesis Y ≠ ∅. Every y ∈ Y satisfies y ≠ x: for y = x both sides of the defining inequality equal 0 (|P(0)| = 0 = (s/4)·0), and 0 < 0 is false. Hence |y − x| > 0 for every y ∈ Y. Also |y − x| ≤ R for every y ∈ Y, because Y ⊆ S.

2. The radius h. The set D := {|y − x| : y ∈ Y} ⊆ ℝ is nonempty (Step 1) and bounded above by R. Let h := sup D. Then:
 (★) |y − x| ≤ h for every y ∈ Y;
 h ≤ R, because R is an upper bound of D;
 h > 0, because for any y₀ ∈ Y we have h ≥ |y₀ − x| > 0.

3. The far point x′. Since h > 0 we have 3h/4 < h = sup D, so some element of D exceeds 3h/4. That is, there is x′ ∈ Y with |x′ − x| > 3h/4. Then x′ ∈ S, |x′ − x| ≤ h by (★), and |P(x′ − x)| < (s/4)|x′ − x|.

4. The slab inclusion. Let z ∈ S with |P(z − x)| < s·h/4. If z = x, then z ∈ {x} and we are done. Assume from now on z ≠ x.
 (a) |z − x| ≤ h. Suppose instead |z − x| > h. Since s > 0, |P(z − x)| < s·h/4 < (s/4)|z − x|, so z ∈ Y, and (★) gives |z − x| ≤ h, a contradiction. Consequently:
 - |z − x| ≤ h < 3h, i.e. z ∈ B(x, 3h);
 - |z − x′| ≤ |z − x| + |x − x′| ≤ h + h = 2h < 3h, i.e. z ∈ B(x′, 3h).
 (b) If z = x′, then |P(z − x)| < (s/4)|z − x| ≤ s|z − x|, so z ∈ X_∞(x, s). With (a), z ∈ X_∞(x, s) ∩ B(x, 3h).
 (c) If z ∈ X_∞(x′, s), then with (a), z ∈ X_∞(x′, s) ∩ B(x′, 3h).
 (d) Otherwise z ∉ X_∞(x′, s), i.e. s|z − x′| ≤ |P(z − x′)|.
 - Since z − x′ = (z − x) − (x′ − x), linearity and the triangle inequality give |P(z − x′)| ≤ |P(z − x)| + |P(x′ − x)|.
 - The right-hand side is < s·h/4 + (s/4)|x′ − x| ≤ s·h/4 + s·h/4 = s·h/2, using |x′ − x| ≤ h and s > 0.
 - Hence s|z − x′| < s·h/2, and dividing by s > 0 gives |z − x′| < h/2.
 - By the triangle inequality, |z − x| ≥ |x′ − x| − |z − x′| > 3h/4 − h/2 = h/4.
 - Therefore |P(z − x)| < s·h/4 < s|z − x|, i.e. z ∈ X_∞(x, s). With (a), z ∈ X_∞(x, s) ∩ B(x, 3h).
 In every case z ∈ {x} ∪ (X_∞(x, s) ∩ B(x, 3h)) ∪ (X_∞(x′, s) ∩ B(x′, 3h)). The computation in (d) also covers z = x′, since x′ ∉ X_∞(x′, s).

5. Conclusion. The number h from Step 2 and the point x′ ∈ S from Step 3 satisfy 0 < h ≤ R and S ∩ {z : |P(z − x)| < s·h/4} ⊆ {x} ∪ ({y : |P(y − x)| < s|y − x|} ∩ B(x, 3h)) ∪ ({y : |P(y − x′)| < s|y − x′|} ∩ B(x′, 3h)). In Lean the right-hand side is insert x (A ∪ A′), where A = {y | ‖P (y - x)‖ < s * ‖y - x‖} ∩ Metric.ball x (3 * h) and A′ is the same set with x′ in place of x. ∎

Lean pointers. Take h := sSup ((fun y ↦ ‖y - x‖) '' Y). Useful lemmas: le_csSup, csSup_le, exists_lt_of_lt_csSup, map_sub, norm_sub_le, dist_eq_norm, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_union.
proof_key_steps: Y := {y ∈ S : |P(y − x)| < (s/4)|y − x|} is nonempty, avoids x (so |y − x| > 0 on Y), and lies within distance R of x.
h := sup{|y − x| : y ∈ Y} satisfies 0 < h ≤ R and |y − x| ≤ h for all y ∈ Y; choose x′ ∈ Y with |x′ − x| > 3h/4.
Maximality of h: every z ∈ S with |P(z − x)| < s h/4 has |z − x| ≤ h, hence z ∈ B(x, 3h) and |z − x′| ≤ 2h < 3h.
If such a z ≠ x is in the s-cone at x′ it lies in X(x′, 3h, s). Otherwise linearity gives |z − x′| < h/2, hence |z − x| > h/4, |P(z − x)| < s|z − x| and z ∈ X(x, 3h, s).

subproblems.title: Packing disjoint balls centred in an n-dimensional subspace
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^N a linear subspace with dim W = n, and Hⁿ := μHE[n]. Let ι be a type, T ⊆ ι a countable set, w : ι → ℝ^N, ρ : ι → ℝ, w₀ ∈ W and R ∈ ℝ. Assume that for all i ∈ T: w(i) ∈ W, ρ(i) > 0 and B(w(i), ρ(i)) ⊆ B(w₀, R). Assume also that the open balls B(w(i), ρ(i)), i ∈ T, are pairwise disjoint. Then Σ_{i∈T} ρ(i)ⁿ ≤ Rⁿ in [0, ∞], i.e. ∑' i : T, ofReal(ρ(i)ⁿ) ≤ ofReal(Rⁿ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (W : Submodule ℝ (Rn N)), finrank ℝ W = n → ∀ (ι : Type) (T : Set ι) (w : ι → Rn N) (ρ : ι → ℝ) (w₀ : Rn N) (R : ℝ), T.Countable → (∀ i ∈ T, w i ∈ W) → w₀ ∈ W → (∀ i ∈ T, 0 < ρ i) → T.PairwiseDisjoint (fun i ↦ Metric.ball (w i) (ρ i)) → (∀ i ∈ T, Metric.ball (w i) (ρ i) ⊆ Metric.ball w₀ R) → ∑' i : T, ENNReal.ofReal (ρ i ^ n) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is Fact (F2) and Step 7 of the parent proof of bf_coneMass_ball_le: packing disjoint n-balls of W into a larger ball of W (Mattila, Lemma 15.14; Dall'Alba, Lemma 4.6). Here it is stated for an arbitrary countable family. In the parent, ι = ℝ^N, T is the Vitali subfamily, w = W.starProjection, ρ(t) = s·h(t)/20, w₀ = W.starProjection a and R = δ/4.

Claim. Let n, N ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^N a linear subspace with dim W = n, and Hⁿ := μHE[n]. Let ι be a type, T ⊆ ι countable, w : ι → ℝ^N, ρ : ι → ℝ, w₀ ∈ W and R ∈ ℝ. Assume w(i) ∈ W, ρ(i) > 0 and B(w(i), ρ(i)) ⊆ B(w₀, R) for all i ∈ T, and that the open balls B(w(i), ρ(i)), i ∈ T, are pairwise disjoint. Then Σ_{i∈T} ofReal(ρ(i)ⁿ) ≤ ofReal(Rⁿ) in [0, ∞].

Notation.
- B(v, r) is the open ball of ℝ^N.
- For v ∈ W, B_W(v, r) := {u ∈ W : |u − v| < r} is the open ball of W for the restricted Euclidean metric.
- μHE[n]_W is the Euclidean Hausdorff measure of the metric space W, with its Borel σ-algebra.
- Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^N is a measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^N.

1. Trivial case. If T = ∅, the sum is 0 ≤ ofReal(Rⁿ). Otherwise fix i₀ ∈ T. Since w(i₀) ∈ B(w(i₀), ρ(i₀)) ⊆ B(w₀, R), we get 0 ≤ |w(i₀) − w₀| < R, so R > 0.

2. Hⁿ on W is a Haar measure. W, with the restricted inner product, is a finite-dimensional real inner product space with finrank W = n.
- First rewrite n as finrank W, using the hypothesis finrank W = n. Then μHE[finrank W] on W is an additive Haar measure (Mathlib instance MeasureTheory.isAddHaarMeasure_euclideanHausdorffMeasure; equivalently it equals volume, InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
- Put ω := μHE[n]_W(B_W(0, 1)).
- ω > 0, because a Haar measure charges nonempty open sets (Metric.measure_ball_pos).
- ω < ∞, because a Haar measure is finite on balls (measure_ball_lt_top).
- For v ∈ W and r > 0, the scaling law of Haar measures gives μHE[n]_W(B_W(v, r)) = ofReal(rⁿ)·ω (Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos). This needs no nontriviality assumption, so n = 0 is included.

3. Transfer to ℝ^N. The inclusion map W → ℝ^N is an isometry, so Hⁿ(image of A) = μHE[n]_W(A) for every A ⊆ W (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image applied to isometry_subtype_coe). For v ∈ W and r > 0, W ∩ B(v, r) is exactly the image of B_W(v, r): a point z ∈ ℝ^N lies in W ∩ B(v, r) iff z ∈ W and |z − v| < r, and distances in W are those of ℝ^N. Therefore
 (F2) Hⁿ(W ∩ B(v, r)) = ofReal(rⁿ)·ω for all v ∈ W and r > 0.

4. The disjoint pieces. For i ∈ T let Bᵢ := W ∩ B(w(i), ρ(i)). Then:
- Bᵢ is a Borel set, because W is closed (a finite-dimensional subspace; Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional) and balls are open;
- Hⁿ(Bᵢ) = ofReal(ρ(i)ⁿ)·ω by (F2), since w(i) ∈ W and ρ(i) > 0;
- the sets Bᵢ (i ∈ T) are pairwise disjoint, because Bᵢ ⊆ B(w(i), ρ(i)) and these balls are pairwise disjoint;
- Bᵢ ⊆ W ∩ B(w₀, R), because B(w(i), ρ(i)) ⊆ B(w₀, R).

5. Additivity. T is countable, so countable additivity of Hⁿ on pairwise disjoint Borel sets (measure_biUnion), monotonicity, and (F2) for v = w₀ ∈ W and r = R > 0 give
 (Σ_{i∈T} ofReal(ρ(i)ⁿ))·ω = Σ_{i∈T} ofReal(ρ(i)ⁿ)·ω = Σ_{i∈T} Hⁿ(Bᵢ) = Hⁿ(⋃_{i∈T} Bᵢ) ≤ Hⁿ(W ∩ B(w₀, R)) = ofReal(Rⁿ)·ω.
 The first equality is ENNReal.tsum_mul_right.

6. Cancellation. Since 0 < ω < ∞, the factor ω can be cancelled in [0, ∞]. This gives Σ_{i∈T} ofReal(ρ(i)ⁿ) ≤ ofReal(Rⁿ), i.e. ∑' i : T, ENNReal.ofReal (ρ i ^ n) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n). ∎
proof_key_steps: If T = ∅ the sum is 0. Otherwise a nonempty ball B(w(i₀), ρ(i₀)) ⊆ B(w₀, R) forces R > 0.
After substituting n = finrank W, μHE[n] on W is an additive Haar measure, so μHE[n]_W(B_W(v, r)) = rⁿ·ω with ω := μHE[n]_W(B_W(0, 1)) ∈ (0, ∞).
The inclusion W → ℝ^N is an isometry and W ∩ B(v, r) is the image of B_W(v, r), so Hⁿ(W ∩ B(v, r)) = rⁿ·ω for v ∈ W and r > 0.
The sets W ∩ B(w(i), ρ(i)), i ∈ T, are pairwise disjoint Borel subsets of W ∩ B(w₀, R). Countable additivity gives ω·Σρ(i)ⁿ ≤ ω·Rⁿ.
